decision_reason: LiteLLM is a BerriAI-developed AI gateway that the City of Munich documents using for its own MUCGPT and other AI applications. That is public-sector use of an independently developed product, not government authorship, commissioning, funding or stewardship. The public source, separately scoped MIT core grant, active distribution and municipal use are recorded, but the government-provenance check fails. No exact catalog match found; no catalog entry added.

government_provenance.note: Munich's first-party page explicitly says the City uses LiteLLM as a gateway for its own applications; it does not claim to have created, funded or commissioned the software. The canonical repository's root LICENSE carries Berri AI copyright (https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/main/LICENSE), and the project is owned/maintained by private company BerriAI. A Munich use-catalog entry is not product provenance.

public_source.note: The publicly accessible canonical repository contains the active Python library/gateway source, deployment package, tests, build files and documentation. It is not merely the City's deployment configuration.

eligible_license.note: The direct root grant explicitly applies OSI-approved MIT to repository content outside `enterprise/`; content under `enterprise/` is separately governed by `enterprise/LICENSE` (https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/main/enterprise/LICENSE), a non-OSI commercial/source-available grant. This is a clearly scoped mixed-license product; only the MIT-covered core is eligible, and the enterprise subtree is excluded from any OSS license claim.

primary_evidence.note: The official City of Munich page describes the gateway's role in MUCGPT and other City applications; the official docs provide current setup/user guidance, and the repository is actively developed and distributed. This documents real independent public-sector reuse and a notable operational product, but not government provenance.

BerriAI added a distinct enterprise/ license scope in 2024; root LICENSE continues to define the boundary. The City of Munich page is evidence of actual use only. No exact catalog match found; no catalog entry added.

The inventory record is a discovery lead, not provenance.
